newsitem.title: USA: CBOE's Chapman to stay on during CEO transition.
newsitem.headline: CBOE's Chapman to stay on during CEO transition.

text.p: Alger "Duke" Chapman, the outgoing chairman and chief executive officer of the Chicago Board Options Exchange, will stay on during the transition period to a new chairman and CEO, the exchange said Wednesday.
In a statement, the exchange confirmed that its board of directors had named Chicago Mercantile Exchange president and CEO William Brodsky to replace Chapman, who will retire in 1997.
Brodsky will assume the office "sometime after the first of the year," the CBOE said.
Chapman has been the CBOE's chairman and CEO since October 1986. Brodsky has served as president and CEO of the CME since 1985 after joining the exchange in 1982.
"Bill Brodsky has proven his leadership abilities by helping to position the CME as an exchange which is synonymous with innovation," Chapman said in the statement.
